name: Chin tucks
instruction: Slide your head straight back, like a double chin.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and your eyes looking straight ahead.
Without tipping your head up or down, glide your chin straight back. Yes, it gives you a double chin.
Hold for 2 or 3 seconds. You should feel a gentle stretch where your skull meets your neck.
Let your head glide forward to neutral. That's one rep.
tip: Keep your eyes level the whole time. If you're nodding down, you're doing a different move.

name: Doorway stretch
instruction: Forearms on a door frame, lean through gently.
steps: Stand in an open doorway. Raise your arms so your elbows are at shoulder height and bent to about 90 degrees.
Rest your forearms flat on each side of the frame, palms facing forward.
Step one foot through and slowly lean forward until you feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Hold for 30 seconds and breathe normally. Step back to release.
tip: Aim for a gentle stretch, not a strain, and don't let your lower back arch. No doorway nearby? Do one arm at a time against a wall corner.

name: Scap squeezes
instruction: Pinch your shoulder blades back and down, then let go.
steps: Sit or stand tall. Let your arms hang, or bend your elbows to about 90 degrees if that's easier.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and slightly down, like you're pinching a pencil between them.
Hold for 2 seconds.
Relax completely, then repeat. Do 15.
tip: Don't shrug your shoulders up toward your ears or push your ribs forward. The move is small and happens in your upper back.

name: Walkaround
instruction: Get up and walk. Refill your water, rest your eyes.
steps: Stand up and walk anywhere for 2 minutes. A lap around the room or a water refill both count.
Let your arms swing and your shoulders drop.
On the way, look at something at least 20 feet away for about 20 seconds to give your eyes a break.
tip: Leave your phone at the desk. This one only works if your eyes get a break too.

name: Thoracic extension
instruction: Hands behind your head, arch back over your chair.
steps: Sit all the way back so the top of your chair's backrest touches your mid back, just below your shoulder blades.
Lace your fingers behind your head with your elbows pointing forward. Your hands support your neck, they don't pull it.
Gently lean back over the backrest, lifting your chest toward the ceiling.
Pause for a breath, then sit back up. Do 10.
tip: Bend from your upper back, not your lower back or neck. If your chair reclines or rolls, brace it against something first or skip this one.

name: Hip flexor stretch
instruction: Split stance, tuck your hips and push them forward.
steps: Stand with one foot a big step in front of the other, both feet pointing forward. Hold your desk if you want.
Bend your front knee a little and keep your back leg long.
Tuck your tailbone under by squeezing the glute on your back leg, then gently shift your hips forward.
You should feel it at the front of your back hip. Hold 30 seconds, then switch legs.
tip: Keep your chest tall. Arching your lower back to go deeper just moves the stretch somewhere it doesn't help.

name: Neck side stretch
instruction: Ear toward shoulder, other shoulder stays down.
steps: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your head to bring your right ear toward your right shoulder. Keep looking forward.
Keep your left shoulder down. For a little more, reach your left hand toward the floor.
Hold for 20 seconds, come back to center slowly, then do the other side.
tip: Don't lift your shoulder up to meet your ear, and don't pull on your head with your hand.

name: Calf raises
instruction: Rise up onto your toes, lower slowly.
steps: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart. Rest a hand on your desk or a wall for balance.
Press through the balls of your feet and rise up as high as you can onto your toes.
Pause for a second at the top.
Lower slowly, taking about 2 seconds, until your heels touch down. Do 20.
tip: Keep your weight over your big toes so your ankles don't roll outward.
